Separate folded CPA variant with both dispersive stages folded. The baseline CPA files and artifacts are retained. Both folded stages use the same 5.65 mm upper/lower separation. The stretcher sits beside the compressor with both input couplers on Y=-300 mm. An additional 1-inch mirror bends its telescope leg while retaining its total optical length and lens focal length; The SHG crystal and downstream output hardware keep their positions; the two 30 mm SHG lenses are now constrained 60 mm apart, with the crystal center midway between them at the lower compressor output height.

The compressor uses one CP_G1 grating four times, one horizontal HRS1015-P01 roof twice, and one vertical HRS1015-P01 roof once. Its nominal axis is Z=12.7 mm, with input/output at Z=15.525/9.875 mm. The horizontal separation is 9.5387 mm; the vertical roof shifts downward by 5.65 mm. All four grating passes are intentionally off axis, at the centers of the four quadrants of the 30.8 x 11.3 mm clear aperture: local face offsets (+/-7.7, +/-2.825) mm.

The horizontal roof's nominal virtual fold plane is 430 mm beyond the first grating hit. Its entrance plane is 417.3 mm away, accounting for the measured roof's 12.7 mm internal axial depth. Actual path lengths include the finite roof path and lateral walkoff; a nominal 860 mm span is not imposed as a chief-ray length.

The compressor input coupler, waveplate and ordinary half-inch CP_M1 mirror in POLARIS-K05VS2 are at Y=-300 mm. CP_M1 is centered at (320, -300, 15.525) mm. The vertical roof entrance is at Y=-100 mm, between the grating and D pickoff, and its physical axis is offset -5 mm along local Y from the displaced return ray. The vertical roof is intentionally off axis; its revised integral stops are 2.54 mm above the seating floor. A 25.4 mm PFD10-03-P01 in KM100DL remains at (320, -220, 9.875) mm, steering the fourth grating pass into SHG. The horizontal roof is entered through B first. Both straight-through beams are checked against the vertical roof with 1 mm radius probes, along with the pickoff and steering-mirror bypass checks.

The stretcher grating is positioned at X=950 mm and its input coupler line at Y=-300 mm. These input-section anchors position the folded stretcher beside the compressor. Its coupler is at X=770 mm, alongside the compressor coupler at X=500 mm. The shared baseplate is regenerated around the closer hardware footprints.

One physical ST_G2 grating and one 25.4 mm ST_L2 lens in a POLARIS-L1G mount are each used four times. The lens focal length is 500 mm, its center is Z=12.7 mm, and the upper/lower beams pass at Z=15.525/9.875 mm. The grating is centered at the lens axis height; its four passes are intentionally off axis.

An additional upright 25.4 mm ST_Bend mirror in POLARIS-K1VS2 turns the telescope leg by 90 degrees, 325 mm axially after the lens. The existing upright 25.4 mm ST_Fold end mirror is 175 mm farther along the folded axis, normal to that nominal axis rather than the sloping incident ray. The two axial lengths total 500 mm and preserve the entire pre-bend ray length. ST_Bend has four intentionally off-axis encounters. The grating-to-lens gap remains 70 mm; finite sloping ray lengths are traced.

The lower return traverses the same lens and grating, then a 25.4 mm PFD10-03-P01 D-shaped mirror in a KM100D mount selects it. The optical datum is 1 mm below the straight edge. The upper path clears the open half; a 1 mm radius clearance probe is checked against the optic and mount.

The D pickoff is 75 mm before the grating. The VA100 is 75 mm after the pickoff, followed 75 mm later by the existing 25.4 mm ST_M1 retroreflector in a POLARIS-K1VS2 mount. The return retraces the entire folded path to the launching coupler.

The upper input steering mirror is 225 mm before the grating; the FBR half-wave plate is 150 mm before it. The integral-lens fiber coupler is 180 mm from that steering mirror. All starter distances and the 2.825 mm lens offset are editable in generate.py and the schematic poses.

The plate top remains Z=3 mm; thickness is 60 mm and the underside is Z=-57 mm. CP_HRoof sits on an XR25C stage recessed to Z=-39 mm, preserving the original optical alignment. The 100 x 70 x 16 mm moving adapter contains the original integral horizontal-roof supports and M2 clamp tap. Four selected existing platform holes receive 1/4-20 x 5/8-inch cap screws. Travel is editable over +/-12.5 mm along the roof optical axis. The deeper stock retains material under the four 12 mm stage-base taps and their drill tips. D-mirror recesses follow the mount axes with a uniform 5 mm offset on every side of the complete holder envelope, including the front mounting area and actuator knobs. Each uses one rectangular pocket without a separate rear extension. Seats and drilling positions are unchanged. Both one-inch D holders use two 2 mm x 5 mm rear-contact locating pins per mount, 22 mm apart, with 4 mm straight plate bores and 1 mm projection above each recess floor. Purchased mounts remain upright and use their real seats, recessed where required; no floating mounts or unspecified spacers are introduced.

SHG lens separation is constrained to 60 mm with the physical crystal center at the midpoint: 30 mm from each lens for the defaults. The input lens is at X=130 mm, the crystal center at X=100 mm and the output lens at X=70 mm. Input lens to crystal center is an explicit 30 mm schematic length constraint. Each output wavelength starts at the physical crystal exit, 13.7 mm after the center, with an explicit 16.3 mm exit-to-lens constraint. The folded CAD builder additionally validates the shared 60 mm span, midpoint and exit alignment across wavelength files before export. Both SHG focal lengths remain 30 mm; lens-mount facing directions and downstream optics are retained.

VA100 slit width is provisionally 1 mm. Beam waists and powers remain illustrative. Native and schematic traces use the existing ideal thin-lens, mirror and grating models; no detailed aberration, pulse dispersion, gain, SHG efficiency or phase matching is predicted.

The output dichroic reflects 775 nm and transmits 1550 nm through an ideal 3 mm, n=1.5 plate. The exact coating/optic is unselected. The residual 1550 nm path retains its half-inch mirror and integral-lens coupler; fiber cables and the EDFA package are omitted.

The rear 1550 nm receiving leg includes SHG_IR_HWP1 in an FBR mount and SHG_IR_PBS1, a 12.7 mm polarizing cube in the existing integral displacement PBS holder. Editable starter spacings are 30 mm mirror-to-waveplate, 30 mm waveplate-to-PBS and 60 mm PBS-to-coupler. The straight transmitted port continues toward -Y into Residual_1550; the reflected port travels 220 mm toward +X to a half-inch POLARIS-K05VS2 mirror, turns toward +Y for 110 mm to a half-inch POLARIS-L05G lens with 30 mm focal length, and ends at the bracketed Newport 818-BB-30 Pickoff_1550 detector 30 mm after the lens. The receiver outward axis points toward -Y. Its plate recess adds 50% to the ordinary transverse width (32.25 mm extra, 96.75 mm total with default clearance) by extending only local +Y on the BNC side, preserving the opposite wall, axial walls, floor and drilling positions. Its 25.4 mm-height bracket is recessed to retain the 9.875 mm beam datum; existing coupler and SHG hardware positions are retained. The half-wave plate fast-axis starter is 22.5 degrees and the reflected PBS polarization axis is 0 degrees. Polarization/power division uses the existing ideal Jones model, not a selected 1550 nm cube coating, validated coupled-mode overlap or detector-response calculation. The detector external entrance datum is at the nominal focal plane; its internal photosensitive depth and finite-beam clipping are not modeled.
All delivered beam solids are constant-width center-ray guides. The plate and drilling are a provisional review draft.
